simplified_form.program: NCR Water Quality and Urban Ecosystem Management Program
simplified_form.remarks: Implementation is generally on schedule. Minor delays were encountered due to right-of-way coordination, weather disturbances, and the relocation of utilities near selected riverbank sites. Coordination with concerned LGUs and national agencies is ongoing.
simplified_form.location: Pasig City, Marikina City, Quezon City, and communities along the Marikina and Pasig River systems
simplified_form.objective: To improve urban river water quality, reduce the amount of solid waste entering major waterways, strengthen flood resilience, restore riverbank ecosystems, and increase community participation in environmental protection.
simplified_form.description: The project will rehabilitate selected urban waterways through riverbank stabilization, solid-waste interception facilities, water-quality monitoring stations, riparian vegetation planting, and community-based river management activities. It also includes drainage-outfall assessment and public information campaigns on proper waste disposal.
simplified_form.projectActivity: Metro Manila Urban River Rehabilitation and Flood Resilience Project

priorityAnalysisFacts.readinessNotes: Feasibility study, environmental assessment, preliminary engineering designs, implementation schedule, and cost estimates have been completed. Priority locations were validated, initial permits and LGU endorsements were secured, and procurement documents are being finalized. Stakeholder consultations included women, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and households located near the affected waterways.

simplified_form.physicalAccomplishment: As of the latest monitoring period, the project has achieved 68% physical completion. Twelve solid-waste interception facilities were installed, 18 kilometers of riverbanks were rehabilitated, 25 water-quality monitoring stations were activated, and approximately 45 hectares of riparian areas were planted with native vegetation.
simplified_form.financialAccomplishment: A total of ₱590,000,000 has been obligated and ₱535,000,000 has been disbursed, representing approximately 83.69% and 75.89% of the approved project funding, respectively.

The Regional Development Council – National Capital Region (RDC-NCR) conducted the Sectoral Committee Meeting for the Economic and Environment Development Committee and Infrastructure Development Committee on 23 April 2025.

The consultation meeting aimed to present the Regional Project Monitoring and Evaluation System (RPMES) input forms and discuss and gather member agencies’ inputs for the relevant chapters of the Regional Development Plan for the NCR Midterm Update 2023–2028.

The meeting was led by the Co-Chairpersons of the Economic and Environment Development Committee, Acting Regional Director Jay A. Acar of the Department of Trade and Industry-NCR and SAVP Orliber Paule of SM Prime, together with the Co-Chairpersons of the Infrastructure Development Committee, SAVP Anton V. Calagu of Megaworld Corporation.

The meeting was also participated in by representatives from government agencies, local government units, the private sector, and non-government organizations.

fields.title: 𝐑𝐃𝐂-𝐍𝐂𝐑 𝐒𝐄𝐂𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐀𝐋 𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐌𝐈𝐓𝐓𝐄𝐄 𝐌𝐄𝐄𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆
fields.summary: he RDC-NCR conducted a Sectoral Committee Meeting on 23 April 2025 to present RPMES input forms and gather agency inputs for the NCR Midterm Update 2023–2028.
fields.body:
The Regional Development Council – National Capital Region (RDC-NCR) conducted the Sectoral Committee Meeting for the Economic and Environment Development Committee and Infrastructure Development Committee on 23 April 2025.

The consultation meeting aimed to present the Regional Project Monitoring and Evaluation System (RPMES) input forms and discuss and gather member agencies’ inputs for the relevant chapters of the Regional Development Plan for the NCR Midterm Update 2023–2028.

The meeting was led by the Co-Chairpersons of the Economic and Environment Development Committee, Acting Regional Director Jay A. Acar of the Department of Trade and Industry-NCR and SAVP Orliber Paule of SM Prime, together with the Co-Chairpersons of the Infrastructure Development Committee, SAVP Anton V. Calagu of Megaworld Corporation.

The meeting was also participated in by representatives from government agencies, local government units, the private sector, and non-government organizations.
